rule.title: High Cohesion within Domain Modules
rule.statement: Modules must exhibit high functional cohesion, where all classes, services, and schemas within a module contribute directly to a single well-defined business domain.
rule.rationale: Low cohesion distributes related business concepts across unrelated folders, increasing cognitive load and causing scattered multi-file edits for a single requirement modification.
rule.implementation_guidance: Colocate routes, controllers, services, validation schemas, and types within src/modules/<feature>/.

forbidden.example: A generic utils/ folder containing chunkDocument(), calculateTax(), and renderNavbar() in the same file.

preferred.example: src/modules/documents/ containing documents.service.ts, documents.routes.ts, documents.validation.ts, documents.types.ts

source.evidence_quote: Cohesion refers to what extent the parts of a module should be contained within the same module. High cohesion means elements are strongly related and focused on a single task.

rule.title: Low Coupling and Explicit Module Contracts
rule.statement: Inter-module dependencies must be strictly decoupled and accessed exclusively through exported public service interfaces or event contracts, never reaching into internal sub-paths.
rule.rationale: Direct deep imports create hidden connascence and fragile coupling, causing internal refactorings of one module to cascade into compilation failures across the codebase.
rule.implementation_guidance: Export a single index.ts or clear Service class per module. Never deep-import into internal helpers of another module.

source.evidence_quote: Coupling measures the degree of interdependence between software modules; low coupling represents a good design that supports high maintainability.

rule.title: Eliminate Connascence of Execution Order
rule.statement: Public service methods must not require external callers to invoke separate methods in an undocumented chronological sequence to produce a valid domain state.
rule.rationale: Connascence of Execution forces external callers to understand internal operational mechanics, leading to uninitialized state bugs and race conditions.
rule.implementation_guidance: Combine sequential steps into a single atomic method or use Builder/Factory patterns with validated completion.

forbidden.example: service.upload(); service.parse(); service.embed(); // Caller must remember the exact sequence

source.evidence_quote: Connascence of Execution occurs when the order of execution between multiple components matters. Architects should strive to minimize non-local connascence.

rule.title: Modular Monolith Domain-Driven Partitioning
rule.statement: Monolithic backends must partition code by domain/feature boundaries rather than technical layers, encapsulating data schemas, logic, and endpoints together.
rule.rationale: Domain partitioning allows individual features to evolve independently, maintains high cohesion, and simplifies future extraction into separate services.
rule.implementation_guidance: Group code under src/modules/auth/, src/modules/documents/, src/modules/rag/, and src/modules/chat/.

forbidden.example: src/controllers/ (all controllers), src/services/ (all services) in flat horizontal buckets.

preferred.example: src/modules/rag/ containing vector services, chunking logic, and similarity query routes.

source.chapter: Chapter 11: The Modular Monolith Architecture Style
source.evidence_quote: The modular monolith architecture style emphasizes domain partitioning... components are grouped by business domains rather than technical capabilities.
